clue.text: Vitality of English model occupied by publicity

indicators.note: a place occupied by something has that thing sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for English
to sit is to pose as an artist's model
public relations, the business of publicity

explanation.surface: An English fashion model's energy is swamped by media attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' reads as a person on a catwalk, but here it is the verb for posing.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is borrowed French for liveliness of mind and spirit, a close synonym for energetic sparkle.

clue.text: The answer is to be finally solved, for example

definitions.text: The answer is to be finally solved, for example

blocks.clueFragment: The answer is to be finally solved
blocks.note: surface reading: the puzzle answer is to be worked out at last

blocks.clueFragment: to be finally solved, for example
blocks.note: setter's reading: 'to be' and 'solved' are prised apart by an adverb, the grammatical fault named by the answer

explanation.surface: A solver is promised the answer will eventually be cracked.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is its own example: 'finally' sits between 'to' and the rest of the verb, so the clue contains a split infinitive.
explanation.definitionFit: A split infinitive places an adverb between 'to' and its verb, exactly what the phrase in the clue does.

clue.text: Either way, it pings your location back

definitions.text: Either way, it pings your location back

blocks.note: surface reading: a phone app sending your position
setter's reading: a detection system bouncing signals, whose name reads the same in both directions

explanation.surface: A device that reports where you are, whichever way you go.
explanation.walkthrough: The word reads the same forwards and backwards, just as its signal returns to the sender; 'Either way' points to that symmetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar bounces radio pulses off objects and times the echo, revealing their position.

clue.text: Where customs are surprisingly bothered by river

indicators.note: a surprising outcome is unexpected, hinting the letters will turn up in an unlooked-for order

blocks.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Local traditions are unexpectedly disturbed by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Customs' looks like traditions, but it means the officials checking goods at a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Customs posts are found at a national frontier, where travellers' goods are inspected on crossing.

clue.text: Musical territory initially extended!

blocks.note: first meaning: the Rodgers and Hammerstein stage show
second meaning: a US state whose postal abbreviation, written out in full, is the name

explanation.surface: A show about a frontier land that keeps growing at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The state's abbreviation is OK, its initials; extend those letters to the full name and you have OKLAHOMA, which was also once Indian Territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma is both a famous Broadway show and an American state formed from earlier frontier lands.

clue.text: Object of advice from Shakespeare about being straight?

definitions.text: Object of advice from Shakespeare about being straight?

blocks.clueFragment: advice from Shakespeare about being straight
blocks.note: surface reading: the Bard urging honesty or plain dealing
setter's reading: the grammatical object in Polonius's line 'to thine ... be true' in Hamlet

explanation.surface: Shakespeare counsels us to be honest, and the question is to whom.
explanation.walkthrough: Polonius tells Laertes 'This above all: to thine own self be true'; being true is being straight.
explanation.definitionFit: In Polonius's famous line the thing one must be true to is oneself, phrased with the archaic pronoun form.

clue.text: Perimeter came down, infiltrated by Military Intelligence

indicators.note: something infiltrated has an intruder working inside it

blocks.note: lit, as a bird lit on a branch, means landed
standard abbreviation, as in MI5

explanation.surface: A boundary fence fell after spies got through it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came down' here means landed, as a bird does, rather than collapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is the boundary or outer edge of an area, which is what a perimeter marks.

clue.text: Such coordination needed for effective strike

blocks.note: surface reading: organisation needed before a workers' walkout
setter's reading: hitting a ball cleanly, which needs sight and grip working together

explanation.surface: Union organisers say careful planning is required for industrial action to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests a walkout, but it is a blow at a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand-eye coordination is the ability to guide physical movement by sight, vital in batting or hitting.

clue.text: Language for Whitehall type to take away, perhaps

blocks.note: a senior British civil servant, Whitehall being the seat of government
a Chinese is a common British takeaway meal; 'perhaps' marks it as one example

explanation.surface: A civil servant's lingo for ordering a takeaway meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitehall is the London street of government ministries, and a mandarin is a top official there.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandarin Chinese is the most widely spoken tongue of China, the standard national speech.

clue.text: Bully British legal lord gone astray

indicators.note: something gone astray has wandered off course, so these letters stray into a new order

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for British
as in 'm'lud', the way a barrister addresses a judge
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A British judge has strayed into intimidating people.
explanation.walkthrough: M'lud (my lord) is how British courts address a judge, giving LUD.
explanation.definitionFit: To bludgeon someone is to coerce them by force or threats, which is what a bully does.

clue.text: Mother and grandmother provide a vague timeline

blocks.note: familiar word for mother
familiar word for grandmother; 'and' simply joins the two

explanation.surface: Mum and gran give a hazy sense of when things will happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish for tomorrow, it is used in English to mean some unspecified later time, a deliberately loose schedule.

clue.text: Where criminals are starting to spend time in rehab

indicators.note: the starting part of each following word is what is kept

blocks.note: opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Offenders are beginning a stretch in a recovery clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: Stir is slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is old slang for prison, the place where convicted offenders are locked up.

clue.text: Landlord's position, where conversion is successful?

blocks.note: first meaning: a pub landlord serves from across the counter
second meaning: in rugby, a conversion kick scores if the ball passes above the crossbar

explanation.walkthrough: A landlord here is a pub owner, not a property owner; a rugby conversion is the kick taken after a try.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes the publican's spot facing customers and the path a scoring rugby kick takes between the posts.

clue.text: Drunk in dry section is nasty

indicators.note: a section is a slice cut from a longer run, so the letters lie within the neighbouring words

blocks.note: letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: Someone intoxicated in an alcohol-free zone behaves badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across drUNK IN Dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Unkind and nasty are synonyms, both describing mean or hurtful behaviour toward others.

clue.text: Capture invaders' leader inside stronghold? No way!

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter
the captured pieces are placed within the walls of the stronghold

blocks.note: a fort is a fortified stronghold
to get someone can mean to catch them
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A defender proposes seizing the attackers' commander in the castle, and is told it's impossible.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'No way!' read as part of the story, but the exclamation is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dismissive exclamations refusing a request outright, telling someone there is no chance.

clue.text: What to do, if letter can't be delivered? Study cover

definitions.text: What to do, if letter can't be delivered?

blocks.note: to read a subject is to study it
to dress is to clothe or cover

explanation.surface: Advice on an undeliverable letter, then a note to look at the envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: When post goes astray you write a new destination on the envelope, giving it a fresh delivery address.

clue.text: Heather by lake provides attractive covering

blocks.note: ling is common heather
Lake Erie, one of the Great Lakes; 'by' places it next to the plant

explanation.surface: Heather growing beside a lake makes a pretty ground cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underwear, often designed to be alluring, so a seductive garment worn on the body.

clue.text: Fail with gun reform? It can be rewarding

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician's failed firearms legislation might still pay off.
explanation.definitionFit: Gainful work earns money or profit, so it pays off and is lucrative.

clue.text: Occasion where French is accommodated for balance

indicators.note: an accommodated guest is given room inside

blocks.note: an event is an occasion
the French word for where

explanation.surface: A function hosting French guests aims for equal numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where French' means the French word for where, not a place in France.
explanation.definitionFit: To even out is to make things level or equal, which is to balance them.

clue.text: Pathetic thing with a replacement for old  …

indicators.note: a replacement means one letter is swapped out and another put in its place

blocks.note: an object is a thing
taken as written
standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A sad old item gets swapped for something new, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: In OBJECT, the O (old) is replaced with A. The ellipsis just carries the surface on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Abject describes something wretched and miserable, as is anything pitiful or pathetic.

clue.text: …  working stiffs from Haiti, perhaps

blocks.note: working as in functioning or alive, as in a living language
stiffs is slang for corpses

explanation.surface: Following the previous clue, downtrodden labourers from a Caribbean country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working stiff' is slang for an ordinary labourer, but here the stiffs are corpses that still move: zombies, which come from Haitian vodou.
explanation.definitionFit: Zombies of Haitian folklore are reanimated corpses, bodies that are dead yet walking about.

clue.text: Writer neglected part about style

indicators.note: a part is only a piece of the whole, so the letters lie inside the neighbouring words
about can mean turned round, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: letters running across the two words, before being turned

explanation.surface: A novelist ignored a section dealing with prose style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' and 'neglected' look like a deletion from an author's name, but the letters are simply hidden backwards: wriTER NEGlected.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a category or kind of artistic work, distinguished by its particular manner or form.

clue.text: Spinning line for a boundary return

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so this word is read from the end

blocks.note: taken as written
in cricket a boundary hit clearing the rope scores six

explanation.surface: A cricket ball spinning back from the boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a ball hit over the boundary rope without bouncing scores six runs.
explanation.definitionFit: An axis is the imaginary straight line around which a body rotates, like the Earth turning.

clue.text: Protection for source of maternal bonds?

blocks.note: first meaning: a garment worn to keep clothes clean
second meaning: what the strings come from when a child is tied to its mother's

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'tied to your mother's apron strings' describes someone overly dependent on their mother.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron shields clothing while cooking, and its strings are the idiomatic ties binding a child to mum.

clue.text: Metal container for one doubly fine light meal

indicators.note: a container holds something, so the metal wraps around the next pieces

blocks.note: tin is a metal
Roman numeral one
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine, doubled

explanation.surface: A tin box holds a single, excellent snack.
explanation.walkthrough: A tiffin is also a metal lunchbox in India, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffin is an Anglo-Indian word for a light midday lunch or snack.

clue.text: Protest turning to take on mean sort of bandit  …

indicators.note: turning round means reading the word in the opposite direction
to take something on is to take it in, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: a demo is a protest march
near is a dated word for stingy

explanation.surface: A demonstration turns to confront a nasty kind of outlaw.
explanation.walkthrough: A one-armed bandit is a slot machine, named for its lever and for taking your money.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-armed bandit is a fruit machine; the phrase names a particular kind of so-called bandit.

clue.text: …  determined he will shortly corrupt

blocks.note: the contraction he'll
bent is slang for dishonest or corrupt

explanation.surface: Continuing the bandit theme: resolved, he will soon go bad.
explanation.walkthrough: Bent is British slang for crooked, as in a bent copper.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell-bent means fiercely set on doing something regardless of consequences, so resolved or determined.

clue.text: Poles central to fat star's decline

indicators.note: something central to another sits in its middle, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: suet is hard animal fat
north and south, the two poles

explanation.surface: A celebrity's fall from grace has opposing camps focused on their weight.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun is our star, and its daily sinking below the horizon is the evening descent.
